title: Semantic HTML
description: Understand the importance of semantic elements and how they help create meaningful and accessible HTML documents.

lessons.title: What is Semantic HTML?
lessons.content: Semantic HTML uses elements that clearly describe their meaning in a human- and machine-readable way. This improves accessibility, SEO, and code clarity.

lessons.title: Benefits of Semantic Markup
lessons.content: Semantic elements improve screen reader support, make documents easier to maintain, and enhance SEO by giving structure to the content.

lessons.title: Common Semantic Elements
lessons.content: Some key semantic tags include `<header>`, `<footer>`, `<article>`, `<section>`, `<aside>`, and `<main>`. These define the role of each block of content.

lessons.title: Nesting Semantic Elements Correctly
lessons.content: Semantic tags can be nested meaningfully. For example, a `<section>` can contain `<article>`, and each `<article>` can have its own `<header>` and `<footer>`.

lessons.title: Semantic HTML vs. Non-Semantic HTML
Improving SEO with Semantic Tags
lessons.content: Search engines use semantic tags to better understand your content. Proper use of `<article>`, `<header>`, and heading tags can boost SEO performance.

lessons.title: Semantic HTML Best Practices
lessons.content: Use the most specific and meaningful tag available, avoid div soup, and maintain logical document structure to improve accessibility and maintainability.
